study_identification_part.si4_title: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives: to parameterize cortical thickness in ASD as an individualized metric of atypicality relative to age-related norms, and to examine heterogeneity.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We examined how cortical thickness (CT) in ASD can be parameterized as an individualized metric of atypicality relative to typically-developing (TD) age-related norms. ... This work showcases an individualized approach for understanding ASD heterogeneity...

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses the ABIDE datasets (open datasets). It cites the original publication (Di Martino et al., 2014). It describes inclusion/exclusion criteria applied in this study (males only, age matching, image quality checks via Euler index).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: To achieve this, we utilized the ABIDE datasets (ABIDE I and II; 15)... Normative modelling of agerelated CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group... We chose to exclude the top 10% of subjects with an extreme Euler index... With the inclusion of motion we also excluded individuals for which no resting-state fMRI was available.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Bethlehem2020.pdf.md: Methods - Participants; Methods - Imaging processing and quantification

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: While the study acknowledges site effects and includes site as a random effect in the conventional case-control analysis, it does not explicitly describe addressing site effects (e.g., harmonization, site as covariate) in the construction of the normative model itself (LOESS regression on age). The normative model was built using the pooled TD group, potentially neglecting the large site effects mentioned.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Normative modelling of agerelated CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group... We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS)... To align the TD and ASD groups, both were binned into one-year age bins. ... As a result, we observed that site had a large effect on explaining variance in CT...
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Bethlehem2020.pdf.md: Methods - Age-related normative modelling; Discussion
